scoring_justification: Final temperature is recomputed from the agent's raw temperature series and compared to digitised Fig. 2 values; structural checks verify adiabatic monotonicity and isothermal oscillation without relying on self-reported metrics.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference final temperatures for strain rates 1e-2 and 1e0
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Digitised from Fig. 2 of the paper, confirmed by reference simulation
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values taken from the convergence plateau in the reference solution that emulates the paper's reported behaviour; consistent with Fig. 2.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The numbers match the temperature plateau shown in the paper's convergence plot; they are not arbitrary but correspond to the published result within reading error.

hidden_assets.purpose: Structural thresholds for strong coupling case (monotonicity and oscillation)
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from the paper's description of stable (adiabatic) versus unstable (isothermal) behaviour.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Thresholds chosen so that the adiabatic split exhibits no oscillation >1 K while the isothermal split shows standard deviation >3 K, matching the qualitative statements in the paper.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These thresholds are based on the paper's own characterisation of the two splits; they are not arbitrary and the reference solution respects them.

outputs.description: Temperature at the inner face of the thick-walled cylinder for two strain rates, each run's complete time history. The final time-step temperature is compared to a hidden reference value from the paper.
Temperature evolution at inner face for strongly coupled case, comparing adiabatic and isothermal splits. Checker verifies monotonic adiabatic curve and oscillatory isothermal curve.

output_contract.notes: The checker extracts the final temperature from the first CSV for each strain rate and compares to a hidden digitised value from the paper's Fig. 2 (±5% tolerance). For the second CSV, it verifies that the adiabatic temperature is monotonic (no oscillation amplitude >1 K) while the isothermal temperature shows a standard deviation >3 K.
